findings.claim: In February 2023 OSHA fined Mars Wrigley more than $14,500 after two workers from an outside contractor fell into a partially filled chocolate tank at its Elizabethtown, Pennsylvania plant in June 2022. OSHA said the workers were not authorised to work in the tanks and had not been trained on the equipment's safety procedures.

A November 2023 CBS News investigation reported children, some as young as five, working on every Ghanaian farm it visited that supplies Mars, and found names on Mars-linked child labour monitoring lists that were inaccurate or fabricated. Mars said it condemns child labour, was not given details in advance, and that more needs to be done.

In December 2017 the FTC finalised a consent order requiring Mars to divest 12 specialty and emergency veterinary clinics as a condition of its $9.1 billion acquisition of VCA, after alleging the deal would lessen competition in 10 US localities. This was a negotiated order, not a court finding.

Mars reports a 16.9% absolute cut in value-chain greenhouse gas emissions from 2015 to 2025 and a 42.6% cut in Scope 1 and 2, against a target of 50% for the value chain by 2030. The figures are self-reported, and neither source cites independent assurance.

In March 2026 Bryn Mawr College announced a $10 million gift from trustee emeritus Jacqueline Badger Mars to support undergraduate scholarships, with a focus on need-based aid. The college says she has given the gift and mentions no pledge or payment schedule.

ecology.reason: Mars is a global food, confectionery and pet care group, a material footprint under the rubric. It reports a 16.9% absolute cut in value-chain emissions since 2015, self-reported, against a 50% target for 2030. No major environmental incident was found in this research.

social.reason: OSHA fined Mars Wrigley in 2023 after two untrained contractor workers fell into a chocolate tank at its Pennsylvania plant. CBS News reported in 2023 child labour on Ghanaian farms supplying Mars and flawed monitoring lists; Mars condemned child labour. No official child labour finding against Mars was found.

legal.reason: Regulatory actions at company level: an FTC consent order, a settlement, requiring divestment of 12 veterinary clinics to clear the VCA purchase (2017), and an OSHA penalty of more than $14,500 (2023). No court finding or personal matter was found.

unresolved.reason: CBS News reporting in 2023 questioned the accuracy of child labour monitoring lists in Mars's Ghana supply chain, finding listed children still working and some fabricated names. This rests on reporting, not an official finding.

proposal.counterweights: Mars reports a 16.9% absolute cut in value-chain emissions since 2015 (self-reported). Jacqueline Mars gave Bryn Mawr College $10 million for need-based scholarships in 2026.
proposal.rationale: Legal 0 to 1: the FTC divestiture order and an OSHA penalty are regulatory actions naming Mars. Unresolved 0 to 1: concerns about child labour monitoring raised only by CBS reporting, rubric level 1. Social and ecology keep their values on documented findings. Politics not checked: OpenSecrets was not reachable.

results.comment: Rewritten: the AP report gives the penalty as 'more than $14,500', not $14,502, and does not say the violation was classed as serious; both details removed. Contractor workers, June 2022 incident, lack of authorisation and training are confirmed.

CBS News, 29 Nov 2023: children as young as 5 found on each Mars-supplying farm visited; listed children still working and some names outright fabrications on monitoring lists obtained from a whistleblower. Mars's statement condemns child labour, says CBS gave no details in advance, and that more needs to be done. Company level, investigative reporting.

FTC release, 19 Dec 2017: final order to settle charges, 12 clinics in 10 localities, $9.1bn VCA deal, complaint alleged substantially lessened competition for specialty and emergency veterinary services. Settlement, not a finding; the claim says so.

ConfectioneryNews (17 Jun 2026) gives 16.9% cumulative value-chain cut and 42.6% Scope 1-2 cut in 2025 against 2015; Mars's 2024 release gives the 50% by 2030 target. Company-reported figures, no independent assurance cited in either; labelled self-reported.

Rewritten: the college page (4 Mar 2026) says she 'has generously gifted' $10 million; it does not itself contrast this with a pledge, so the claim now says what the page states. Individual level, names her.
